rationale: AMBIGUOUS REFERENCE TARGET, DISAMBIGUATED BY THE COMPILATION UNIT (java lane, 2026-11-17). Sub-directory fixture, so the runner supplies a COMPLETE project index (JAVA_DECLARATION_SPEC). The project declares the simple name `Filter` THREE times: top-level in Filter.java, nested in ToolOwners, and nested in ToolOwners.Other. A bare reference to `Filter` is therefore genuinely ambiguous (symbolCounts > 1) and the indexer cannot pick one. JLS 7.5.1 resolves it for this compilation unit: the single-type import binds the simple name to the top-level Filter, and the declared-type reference must be re-spelled to that path. POSITIVE: the references edge for the field's declared type names the qualified path and carries importedFrom. NEGATIVE CONTROL: without the fix the target stays the bare leaf `Filter`, which the indexer cannot resolve against three declarations, so this fixture fails without the change and passes with it. The import MENTION edge is deliberately NOT re-spelled: its target is the module path already.
